narratives.Overview:
- **R0 — Closed instruction class.** First ship stops every agent-runnable instruction to run bare `gh auth status`: preamble `:472` / `:469`, pack JSON skills 8/9/17 plus rendered SKILL.md, swarm `core-phase-3.md:78/:81`, `gh-rest.ts` hints, and the `swarm_phase3_step1a_sandbox_auth_token_present` pin. Edit the pack JSON. Recut that pin in the same change. Stay-list: `content/commands.md`, `content/contracts/scm-readiness.md`, `content/scm/github.md:339`, `content/patterns/multi-agent.md:106` plus `content/packs/patterns/patterns-pack-0.1.json:84`, `tasks/verify.yml:227`, preamble `:463` (`!` line, "the host's `gh auth status` token") beside `:465`. Prohibitions stay (core-ops `:146`, core-phase-3 `:89`, preamble `:465`, swarm test `:555`, multi-agent.md `:73`). Exclude generated `SPECIFICATION.md` or re-render it in the same change. Delete dead constants at `swarm_skill.test.ts:114-137` with the `:539` recut. `extractBoundRemedyHarvest` on this lean body must retain this R0 item; do not write Unchanged-from pointer stubs.

- **R1 — Split usable from identity.** Swarm worker identity keeps `task verify:gh-auth` / `deft github-auth-modes` and drops the extra agent-run of `gh auth status`. Consumer gh-arch / gh-slice "is gh usable?" is `gh api rate_limit` exit code (preamble §7 already names it). `deft scm:status` shallow stays named as the policy-aware probe and refuses `cloud-headless` hosts.yml credentials by design; that refusal is the #3656 / #5016 question, not this P1. Do not add `--github-auth-mode host-gh` to `scm:status` in this PR. Pin `parseLogin` (`github-auth-modes.ts:318-336`) and `formatUserApiFailureDetail` (`:394-405`) so CLI text and JSON never emit raw gh stdout or stderr, including ANSI `/user` JSON. Recut `github-auth-modes.test.ts:263-271` (raw non-JSON stdout as `login`) in the same change. Typed fields stay `resultToDict` keys. Installation identity stays on #3693.

- **R2 — Mechanized scan.** Content-contract over `content/**`, `content/templates/**`, pack JSON, engine `hint`/`remediation` strings, and `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md`. Three line classes: prohibitions stay; descriptions reworded to the verb; imperatives replaced. Banning every occurrence of the string is a miss. Heartbeat: collapse `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:364-366` onto one binding line immediately before the fence at `:368`. Fence body ships `deft github-auth-modes --json` (resolves; satisfies the #3439 spelling oracle). Pin: `bindingFenceCommands("docs/subagent-heartbeat.md")` returns that command; assert the targeted auth command is present before `taskVerbResolves`. A negative fixture with an unknown auth verb must fail. Do not rely on a nonempty-result assertion that still passes on `verify:subagent-alive`. Do not append the file to `SWARM_FILES` and rely on `bindingTaskVerbs`. Also rewrite `:376/:390` off the dead `scripts/github_auth_modes.py` / `scripts/platform_capabilities.py`.

- **R3 — Advisory and floor.** Record GHSA-cg6r-mpgc-h9mm / CVE-2026-64652. Cite the repository advisory URL (`repos/cli/cli/security-advisories/GHSA-cg6r-mpgc-h9mm`), not the global advisory DB. Grow `toolchain-check.ts:24-32` and `:278`: parse the captured `gh --version` line, compare to 2.97.0, warn (advisory id, upgrade path). `toolchain:check` / `check:consumer` get it for free. `verify:tools` / `doctor` get it only if the gh ToolSpec grows a version probe; R3 does not add a new verb and does not spawn a second `gh --version` inside `verify-tools.ts`. Rotation stays operator-facing (CHANGELOG / GHSA cite), not agent-run warn text. Do not keep bare `gh auth status` on the floor.

- **R4 — Token-shaped output invariant.** No deft-emitted `detail` / `remediation` / `login` carries token-shaped text (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`) or raw subprocess streams from `gh auth status` / `gh api user`. Keep the return-code-only pin on the three auth-status call sites. Cover both streams. Align `CREDENTIAL_VALUE_PATTERN` with that prefix set if R4 ships.

- **R5 — Release.** Replace release `:199` with two lines, neither printing a token: (1) `gh api rate_limit` exit code (usable); (2) identity: `task verify:gh-auth -- --repo <owner>/<repo> --expected-login <maintainer>` after R1's `parseLogin` pin lands in the same change, or `gh api user --jq .login` compared to the expected login (preamble `:464`/`:472` already name it). Delete the parenthetical. No dedicated auth gate exists in `packages/core/src/release/`. The pipeline fails at the Step 5 census or tag gate without auth (`pipeline.ts:472`). gh-arch / gh-slice keep `rate_limit` alone.

- **R6 — Remeasure.** Bind the defect as agent-runnable `gh auth status` on every host where gh prints a `Token:` line. Re-measure on a dispatched worker transcript. CHANGELOG notes consumer relief lands after a release pin plus `deft update`. Upstream masking remains a follow-up.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Tickets: using GitHub issues to drive the work. A change is supposed to live on its own branch, and the pull request is supposed to point back at the issue that asked for it.

What a new person hits: The product's own guidance tells an agent to run a GitHub login check that prints a live credential.

Why that ruins the product for them: Following the instructions can leak a token into the chat. A careful person stops and does not resume.

How likely: Medium. It depends on an agent following that guidance. When it happens, it is a trust-ending moment rather than a confusing one.

## Gate stamp

Round-1 ceiling is this write-back plus panel-deposit (spend N≥3). Families: grok, claude (opus), codex.

P1 is the guidance leak, not a deft-engine stdout interpolation. polfer 5780305333 records the adoption-blocker reading: a new person following the product's own instructions prints a live credential.

Re-measured at dispatch SHA `92b74e960919ac41b922abc9e0498b66e4066383` by pin-read. Catalog chip `design-critique:mechanism-shaped` applied via `task scm:issue:design-critique-chip`.

Pin-read:

- `content/skills/deft-directive-gh-arch/SKILL.md:33` still MUST-verifies `gh` with `gh auth status`.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-gh-slice/SKILL.md:44` is the same MUST.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md:199` still MUST-verifies `gh auth status` reports authenticated.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md:78` still requires `gh auth status` for `host-gh`. Line 73 already names `task verify:gh-auth -- --json`. Line 81 still describes the parent shell passing `gh auth status`. Line 89 forbids assuming parent-shell `gh auth status` proves worker readiness. `core-ops.md:146` already points workers at `task verify:gh-auth`.
- `tasks/verify.yml` ships `verify:gh-auth` at this SHA.
- Programmatic sites check return code and keep stdout off the `detail` strings: `packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts:593` and `:613` (`authStatus.returncode !== 0`; details are the literals `injected token present but gh auth status failed in worker` and `gh auth status failed in worker environment`). `packages/core/src/scm/readiness.ts:409` is the same return-code check; `:249` says the probe never echoes token values.

What this P1 is not:

- Not a deft-engine leak of `gh` stdout into error `detail`.
- Not the #3656 / #5016 source-selection recut.
- Not the #3858 credential-class ban.
- Not an upstream-only `cli/cli` masking bug. The issue records that report as a follow-up, not the first ship.

Open forks the critic may take: replace the four MUST surfaces with `task verify:gh-auth` vs a wrapper that never prints `gh` stdout vs a documented prohibition vs keep the command and document the leak; whether `core-phase-3.md:78` "requires `gh auth status`" is still a mandate after the verb exists; whether `verify:gh-auth` itself must be shown never to echo `gh` stdout.

Charter: open critique, round 1, fresh. Input ceiling 5819206261. Reads pinned to `92b74e960`. Upstream `cli/cli` reads are public REST.

## Verdict

The triage P1 is real, and the refutation target fails for guidance surfaces. The fix shape cannot bind as written. It misses the upstream fix, and its surface list is incomplete. Two findings block the design, four sharpen it, and one is a footnote.

## Anchors re-verified

`git show` confirmed each envelope anchor: gh-arch `:33`, gh-slice `:44`, release `:199`, core-phase-3 `:73/:78/:79/:81/:89`, core-ops `:146`, `tasks/verify.yml` `verify:gh-auth`. The runner at `github-auth-modes.ts:118-122` uses `stdio: ["ignore","pipe","pipe"]`. The auth-status failure details at `:598` and `:618` are fixed literals. `readiness.ts:408-412` is also a fixed literal. The "code discards stdout" claim holds.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — Upstream already fixed this, and the fix covers more token types than the issue says

Evidence: `cli/cli` advisory GHSA-cg6r-mpgc-h9mm / CVE-2026-64652 ("Partial token disclosure in `gh auth status` output"). It was published 2026-07-31. Affected versions are `<= v2.96.0`, and the fix is in `v2.97.0`. At tag `v2.91.0`, `pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go` `maskToken` masks only the text after the **last** `_`. At trunk and v2.97.0+, it masks everything after a known prefix. This explains the measurement exactly: about 250 characters visible on a `ghs_<APPID>_<JWT>` token. The advisory also names `github_pat_*` fine-grained PATs, `ghu_*`, and the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` as affected. This host runs `gh 2.88.1`, which is also vulnerable.

Failure mode: The issue's caveat ("specific to long `ghs_` installation tokens … a shorter `gho_` token may mask acceptably") understates the exposure. Local desktops with fine-grained PATs also leak. Proposed step 4 ("report upstream") is moot. A guidance-only fix leaves every other `gh auth status` run exposed on gh < 2.97.0. That includes humans, CI, host tooling, and finding 2's runtime hints.

Disposition consequence: Restate the root cause as "gh < 2.97.0 plus deft guidance that mandates the command". Replace step 4 with "record the advisory". Add a deterministic control: a gh version floor (warn at least) in the existing `verify:tools` / `doctor` path. I found no gh version-floor check in `packages`, `tasks`, or `content` at this SHA. Add rotation remediation from the advisory: `DELETE /installation/token` for installation tokens, and regenerate fine-grained PATs.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The surface inventory misses the highest-fan-out mandate and engine-emitted hints

Evidence:
- `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:472`: `! Still verify identity before GitHub operations: \`gh auth status\` must pass.` Line `:469` also treats a preflight-confirmed `gh auth status` as the host-gh precondition. AGENTS.md requires this preamble verbatim in every implementation-worker dispatch (#954). That makes it the most-executed mandate, and it runs in worker transcripts that parents and siblings read.
- `packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts:274,421,437,447,464,568`: six runtime `hint:` strings say "check gh auth status" / "verify gh auth status". They fire on `gh api` failures, which is exactly when an agent debugs and follows the hint.

Failure mode: Ship the four named surfaces, and the Verification box "No deft guidance surface instructs running bare `gh auth status`" is ticked by hand. Every dispatched worker still runs the command per the preamble. Every REST failure still tells the agent to run it.

Disposition consequence: Add the preamble and the gh-rest hints to the fix list. Replace the manual checkbox with a mechanized scan over `content/**`, `content/templates/**`, and engine `hint`/`remediation` strings. The scan must tell three line classes apart, or it will false-positive or be weakened to pass:
- prohibitions: core-ops `:146`, core-phase-3 `:89`, preamble `:465`, multi-agent `:73`. These stay.
- descriptions of what a verifier checks: core-phase-3 `:78`, `docs/subagent-heartbeat.md:393`, `scm-readiness.md:38`, `commands.md:504`. Reword these to name the verb.
- imperatives to run the command: gh-arch, gh-slice, release, preamble `:472`, and the gh-rest hints. Replace these.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Take the replace-verb fork; check the consumer spelling first

Evidence: `verify:gh-auth` exists and pipes stdio, so it is the right replacement for maintainer and swarm surfaces. But gh-arch and gh-slice are consumer skills. I found no `gh-auth` registration under `packages/cli/src` at this SHA. I searched for the literal `gh-auth`, so this is a weak negative. Consumers without the task include may have no working spelling. On gh 2.91.0, `gh auth status --json hosts` exists (the Exporter path) and drops the token field entirely ("In machine-readable we just drop the token").

Failure mode: Pointing consumer skills at `task verify:gh-auth` gives consumers a verb they cannot run. The agent then falls back to bare `gh auth status`.

Disposition consequence: For consumer surfaces, use the `deft`-spelled verb if it exists. If not, register one, or fall back to `gh auth status --json hosts >/dev/null` with an exit-code check.

Road not taken: prohibition-only, or keep the command and document the leak. Steelman: with a gh ≥ 2.97.0 floor enforced fail-closed, bare `gh auth status` is safe and the guidance could stay. What would flip my verdict: deft controls gh on every host it runs on. It does not. Cursor cloud images pin gh, and consumers choose their own gh. So replace the command and add the floor; do not rely on the floor alone.

### 4. sharpens-framing — The invariant is broader than "no auth-status output in a detail"

Evidence: `github-auth-modes.ts:394-397` `formatUserApiFailureDetail` puts up to 240 characters of raw `gh api user` stdout+stderr into `detail` (`clipFailureText(combinedGhText(proc))`). This is not auth-status output, so the issue's test criterion passes as written.

Failure mode: A future `gh` error message that echoes auth context lands in `detail`, and then in transcripts. The auth-status-only test does not catch this.

Disposition consequence: State the invariant as "no deft-emitted detail/remediation carries token-shaped text". Enforce it with a redaction pass for the prefixes `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, and `github_pat_`, and a test. Keep the return-code-only pin for the three call sites.

### 5. sharpens-framing — The release fallback claim is unverified

Evidence: release `:199` says "(`task release` will refuse otherwise)". I grepped `packages/cli/src/release*.ts` (`release-publish`, `release-e2e`, `release-rollback`) for `auth` and found no auth-status or SCM-readiness check. This is a weak negative, because the check may live in a task wrapper I did not trace.

Failure mode: If the MUST is removed on the strength of that parenthetical, release loses its only auth preflight.

Disposition consequence: Replace the release MUST with the verb, not with a pointer to the parenthetical. Verify or delete the parenthetical.

### 6. sharpens-framing (injection / swarm lens) — Worker transcripts are shared, untrusted input

Evidence: Preamble `:472` runs in workers. Nuclear-family topology (#3155) gives parents and siblings read access to worker DONE messages and transcripts. Remediation at core-phase-3 `:84` already says "without pasting token values into dispatch envelopes".

Failure mode: One worker's leaked `ghs_` token becomes readable by every agent that ingests that transcript. Any agent that pastes debug output into an issue (the issue names this path) publishes it. That makes this a cross-agent credential spill, not a local terminal leak.

Disposition consequence: Put the preamble fix (finding 2) in the first ship, not a follow-up. The re-measure checkbox should cover a dispatched worker transcript, not only a parent session.

### 7. footnote — No embedded instructions found

I found no embedded instructions in the issue body or in-envelope comments. The polfer 5780305333 adoption-blocker reading is a claim, not a command. It is consistent with findings 1 and 2.

The guidance fix is warranted. Reusing `verify:gh-auth` is the strongest starting point, but replacing only the four named surfaces and calling the existing verb wholly output-safe would leave two gaps. This is an open critique of the issue and comments through **5819206261**, against **92b74e960919ac41b922abc9e0498b66e4066383**; no later critic posts were read.

### C1 — blocks-the-design — The four-surface migration misses the worker preamble and the authored skill sources

**Evidence.** A SHA-pinned scan found another operative MUST in [the canonical worker preamble, line 472](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/92b74e960919ac41b922abc9e0498b66e4066383/content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md#L472): identity verification still requires `gh auth status` to pass. The three rendered skills also obtain their unsafe instructions from [the skills pack](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/92b74e960919ac41b922abc9e0498b66e4066383/content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json), at JSON pointers `/skills/8/body`, `/skills/9/body`, and `/skills/17/body`. Their generated-file headers identify that source and `task packs:render`.

**Failure mode.** A worker following its canonical dispatch preamble can still run the bare command after the four listed files are repaired. Editing only rendered skills also allows regeneration to restore the old instructions.

**Disposition consequence.** The first ship needs the authored skill entries, their rendered outputs, the swarm guidance, and the worker preamble. A deterministic content check should reject operative bare-command instructions across the maintained guidance sources and generated guidance. It should permit descriptions of the internally captured probe and explicit prohibitions; banning every occurrence of the string would conflate safe implementation descriptions with executable guidance. The four cited surfaces remain real, but are not an exhaustive repair list.

### C2 — blocks-the-design — The replacement's output guarantee must cover both streams and its API-error branch

**Evidence.** `tasks/verify.yml:217–235` already routes `verify:gh-auth` to `github-auth-modes`. I executed the pinned TypeScript modules in memory with injected subprocess results. All **six** auth-status cases kept a synthetic credential canary out of their returned reports: host-gh and injected-token success/failure, plus shallow readiness success/failure. This supports the issue's narrow claim that those three auth-status sites do not echo their captured output.

However, [formatUserApiFailureDetail](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/92b74e960919ac41b922abc9e0498b66e4066383/packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts#L399) incorporates parsed or raw `/user` output into `detail`. Injecting the same nonsecret canary into either stdout or stderr of a failed `/user` call put it in the result. Calling `githubAuthModesMain` then reproduced the canary on CLI stdout in **both text and JSON modes**, with exit 1. That is a measured output path, not evidence that GitHub normally returns credentials in its errors.

There is also a concrete reason not to suppress stdout alone: [upstream v2.91.0 status rendering](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.91.0/pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go#L301) sends the complete status listing to stderr when any authentication entry produces a final error. A successful account's token line can therefore travel on the error stream.

**Failure mode.** A stdout-only wrapper leaves another transcript channel open. Promoting the current verifier as emitting no subprocess output overstates its guarantee: its downstream diagnostics still copy untrusted command text into the transcript. JSON formatting and truncation do not remove that text.

**Disposition consequence.** Before binding the proposed whole-verb guarantee, define the public output boundary as typed status/identity fields and approved failure diagnostics, with no raw credential-bearing subprocess streams. Pin that boundary at the CLI's text and JSON outputs, including auth-status success/failure and API-error paths, with distinct nonsecret canaries in both streams. If the chosen scope protects only auth-status output, state that narrower guarantee and explicitly retain the API-diagnostic residual; do not certify the whole verb from the three return-code checks.

### C3 — sharpens-framing — Safe verification must preserve worker identity policy, including refusal

**Evidence.** The existing validator already checks the target repository, supports an expected user login, and distinguishes identity failures. ## Summary

`gh auth status` prints a live, usable GitHub credential to stdout in Cursor cloud, and four deft guidance surfaces instruct agents to run it. Agent stdout is recorded in transcripts, so the credential lands in a durable artifact.

Deft already forbids exactly this. `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md:79`:

> token values MUST NOT enter prompts or transcripts

The guidance that mandates `gh auth status` contradicts that rule on any host where `gh`'s default masking is inadequate.

## Measured on a real Cursor cloud VM, 2026-08-23

Observed while taking the #3656 environment measurement ([5389068843](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3656#issuecomment-5389068843)). The measuring agent redacted the value and reproduced no substring of it; no credential material appears in this issue or on that thread.

Cursor cloud authenticates with a `ghs_` **GitHub App installation token** stored in `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`. Default `gh auth status` — no `--show-token` — printed the `Token:` line with roughly **250 characters of the JWT visible and only the final ~23 masked**.

The credential is live: `gh api repos/deftai/directive` succeeds and `rate_limit` reports a core limit of 15000. Anyone reading that transcript has repo access for the token's lifetime.

`gh` version 2.91.0.

## Scope — what does and does not leak

**Deft's own code does not leak it.** Every programmatic call site checks only the return code and discards stdout, and the failure `detail` strings are fixed literals:

- `packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts:183` — `authStatus.returncode !== 0`
- `packages/core/src/intake/github-auth-modes.ts:247` — same
- `packages/core/src/scm/readiness.ts:351` — same

**The guidance surfaces are the exposure.** These instruct a human or agent to run the command in a shell, where stdout is captured by the terminal and the agent transcript:

- `content/skills/deft-directive-gh-arch/SKILL.md:33` — `! Verify gh is authenticated: gh auth status`
- `content/skills/deft-directive-gh-slice/SKILL.md:44` — identical wording
- `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md:179` — `! Verify gh auth status reports authenticated`
- `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md:76` — `host-gh … requires gh auth status`

`gh-arch` and `gh-slice` both carry it as a MUST in Prerequisites, so a conforming agent runs it at skill start on every invocation.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than accepting

Agent transcripts are not a secure store. They are read by other agents, pasted into issues for debugging, attached to bug reports, and retained on disk and in vendor clouds. A credential with repo write access sitting in one is a real exposure, and nothing in the current flow tells the operator it happened.

The blast radius scales with the identity. `content/patterns/multi-agent.md` targets App installation tokens as the preferred worker credential, which is precisely the token shape that reproduces this.

## Not an upstream-only problem

`gh`'s masking of long installation tokens is inadequate and arguably an upstream bug worth reporting. But deft does not need to wait on that. It chooses to mandate the command, and it has a safer surface already: `task verify:gh-auth`, cited at `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-ops.md:142` as the thing workers should run instead of trusting a parent-shell probe.

## Proposed direction

Not yet designed; the shape below is a starting point, not a bound decision.

1. Stop mandating bare `gh auth status` in agent-facing guidance. Point the four surfaces at a deft verb that reports an authenticated boolean and a login without echoing `gh` stdout.
2. If a verb needs the underlying call, keep discarding stdout as the three code call sites already do, and never surface it in an error `detail`.
3. Consider a documented rule that no deft guidance may instruct an agent to run a command that prints credential material, alongside the existing transcript rule at `core-phase-3.md:79`.
4. Report the masking defect upstream to `cli/cli`.

## Verification

- [ ] No deft guidance surface instructs running bare `gh auth status`
- [ ] The replacement reports auth state without emitting `gh` stdout
- [ ] The three programmatic call sites still discard stdout, pinned by a test
- [ ] A test asserts no `detail` or remediation string interpolates `gh auth status` output
- [ ] Re-measured on a Cursor cloud session: no credential material in the transcript
- [ ] Upstream report filed or a decision recorded not to
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` line

## Caveats

Single measurement, one programmatically-dispatched cloud VM, unreplicated. Not measured on local desktop with a keyring PAT, where a shorter `gho_` token may mask acceptably — the finding is specific to long `ghs_` installation tokens and should not be assumed universal.
